text:
Maya: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to lock down semantics for the model release metadata fields. Two areas are blurry: (1) what consumers (clients/runtime) can *rely* on vs advisory signals, and (2) lifecycle transitions (expiry/tombstone/deprecation) and how they affect routing. @Ben @Priya can you weigh in?

Ben: Short answer: be conservative. Make most things advisory except explicit rollout flags. Clients shouldn't auto-migrate based on an opaque 'stability' string alone.

Priya: Agreed. Runtime needs a couple of deterministic hooks though: a machine-readable compatibility key and an optional fallback list. Something like: `compat_hashes: ["abc123", "def456"]` so routing can pick the nearest compatible variant.

Sam: Sketch for a compact schema we can iterate on:
```yaml
pin: 
  id: "org/model@2026-03-02"
  stability: "experimental|stable|legacy"  # advisory
  compat_hashes: ["abc123"]                # deterministic fallback hints
  routing_priority: 10                      # runtime hint (lower = prefer)
  deprecation_date: "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z"
  tombstone: false                          # tombstone vs active
  replaced_by: null                         # id of replacement pin
```

Maya: Nice. A couple of questions: 1) If deprecation_date arrives, do we auto-tombstone or just surface alerts? 2) Should TTL lead to deletion or tombstone?

Ben: Don't auto-delete anything. Operationally dangerous. Preferred flow: on deprecation_date -> mark tombstone=true and set `tombstone_reason` + `last_owner`. Human must approve hard-delete.

Priya: From the serving side, tombstoned pins should still be resolvable for SLO-preserving fallbacks for a grace window (configurable per tenant). So we need `tombstone_at` and `tombstone_grace_seconds`.

Sam: Also add `migration_safety: "soft|hard"` to indicate whether automated roll-forward is safe. Runtimes can use that plus `compat_hashes`.

Maya: Operational fields that surfaced so UIs and alerts can show meaningful info: `created_by`, `last_modified_by`, `last_modified_ts`, `audit_url`.

Ben: One more: `client_contract_version` — a small integer clients can check to decide whether to enable new features tied to the model shape/outputs. This avoids clients guessing from 'stability'.

Priya: Implementation notes for the runtime: keep the routing decision deterministic and fast. Prefer `routing_priority` then `compat_hashes` resolution, then tenancy routing policy. Avoid any heuristic that inspects `migration_notes`.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: rollout-meta-schema-v0.3 applied to staging at 2026-03-02T14:07:00Z :white_check_mark:

Maya: Action items: (1) Priya to add `tombstone_at` and `tombstone_grace_seconds` + runtime integration notes (2) Ben to write tombstone lifecycle doc + no-auto-delete policy (3) Sam to update client lib to read `client_contract_version` and fall back to explicit rollout flags. I'll draft a short follow-up RFC with the proposed fields and examples and ping infra+devex. Target: EOD today. :thumbsup:
